Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft: no 3.2.0 build guide exists for Sorcerer anywhere, so this is constructed from the patch notes rather than copied. The argument is the simplest one on any page in this directory. 3.2.0 cuts Fire builds hard - Firewall and Pyromancy named specifically - and halves the Elemental Constellation legendary node, while in the same patch making Ball Lightning playable again and giving the class a +30% core-stat scalar. The class's carried-forward build is a Fire build built on that halved node. If the patch notes mean what they say, the Sorcerer's 3.2.0 build is a Shock build, and the only Shock skill the notes single out is Ball Lightning. What this page cannot tell you is how good: 'made playable again' is a direction, not a number, and no 3.2.0 source publishes a Ball Lightning damage figure, a skill tree or a paragon layout. Treat every allocation below as a starting shape.

Rotation
  1. Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning held on the pack, Blizzard for the cross-element procs, Teleport out - with Ice Armor and Unstable Currents kept up.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning into the pack, Chain Lightning to finish, Teleport to reposition. Watch attack speed as a damage stat rather than a comfort stat - the Orbital upgrade's damage per second scales with it.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 and Torment 1, or whenever Mrak hands them over, and a first read on whether Ball Lightning's 3.2.0 damage is competitive at all.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning held on the pack, Blizzard for cross-element procs, Teleport out. Run the damage comparison against sorcerer-meta-firewall here.
Move on when [ptr] Ball Lightning measurably out-damaging Firewall on 3.2.0 numbers. If it is not, the hypothesis has failed and the hedge variant is the better answer.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Record the comparison numbers properly.
Move on when [ptr] The comparison is done and this build won. Given how thin the evidence is, that is a genuinely open question.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers and untested on this patch. Both 3.2.0 aggregator class lists put Sorcerer near the bottom (C on one, B on the other) and neither of them is looking at this build. Re-verify everything when Season 15 ships.

Point allocation, in order50 points across 6 nodes

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build of this class anywhere: the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides when the PTR digest was written. InfinityBuilds now carries Season 15 PTR builds, but only Warlock ones. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list knowledge/ptr/season-15.md authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Ball Lightning first with the Orbital upgrade
  2. Charged Bolts as the generator
  3. Chain Lightning for clear while gear is bad
  4. Teleport and Ice Armor for survival
  5. Unstable Currents ranked last, with 3.1.0's diminishing returns on its rank scaling noted

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries, so this is the Season 14 Sorcerer pairing carried over and labelled as such: Subo hired, Raheir reinforcing on Bastion. Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft: no 3.2.0 build guide exists for Sorcerer anywhere, so this is constructed from the patch notes rather than copied. The argument is the simplest one on any page in this directory. 3.2.0 cuts Fire builds hard - Firewall and Pyromancy named specifically - and halves the Elemental Constellation legendary node, while in the same patch making Ball Lightning playable again and giving the class a +30% core-stat scalar. The class's carried-forward build is a Fire build built on that halved node. If the patch notes mean what they say, the Sorcerer's 3.2.0 build is a Shock build, and the only Shock skill the notes single out is Ball Lightning. What this page cannot tell you is how good: 'made playable again' is a direction, not a number, and no 3.2.0 source publishes a Ball Lightning damage figure, a skill tree or a paragon layout. Treat every allocation below as a starting shape.

Rotation
  1. Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning held on the pack, Blizzard for the cross-element procs, Teleport out - with Ice Armor and Unstable Currents kept up.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning into the pack, Chain Lightning to finish, Teleport to reposition. Watch attack speed as a damage stat rather than a comfort stat - the Orbital upgrade's damage per second scales with it.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 and Torment 1, or whenever Mrak hands them over, and a first read on whether Ball Lightning's 3.2.0 damage is competitive at all.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Charged Bolts to generate, Ball Lightning held on the pack, Blizzard for cross-element procs, Teleport out. Run the damage comparison against sorcerer-meta-firewall here.
Move on when [ptr] Ball Lightning measurably out-damaging Firewall on 3.2.0 numbers. If it is not, the hypothesis has failed and the hedge variant is the better answer.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Record the comparison numbers properly.
Move on when [ptr] The comparison is done and this build won. Given how thin the evidence is, that is a genuinely open question.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers and untested on this patch. Both 3.2.0 aggregator class lists put Sorcerer near the bottom (C on one, B on the other) and neither of them is looking at this build. Re-verify everything when Season 15 ships.

Reasoning

Hypothesis[ptr] Sorcerer's 3.2.0 balance pass points at Shock. Fire is cut with two named victims (Firewall, Pyromancy) and the Elemental Constellation legendary node is halved; Ball Lightning is explicitly made playable again; and the +30% core-stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) applies to whichever element you pick. A Ball Lightning build should therefore keep all of the patch's upside and take none of its named downside, which no other Sorcerer build on this patch can say.
Confidencemedium
How to test it[ptr] (1) The number nobody has published: measure Ball Lightning's damage on 3.2.0 against the same character's Firewall. 'Made playable again' could mean anything from competitive to merely not embarrassing. (2) Check whether the Orbital upgrade's damage-per-second still scales with attack speed the way the 3.1.0 feed's own formula does - this repo's value tables record that its published span of 130-173% is exactly 1.44 times attack speed over the 0.90-1.20 range, so attack speed is a damage stat for this skill and should be geared as one. (3) Confirm the Elemental Constellation halving really is the cost it looks like for the Fire build, by comparing this build against sorcerer-meta-firewall on the PTR rather than against its live-season reputation. (4) Soul Splinter: Ball Lightning crits, so Splinter of Anguish and not Splinter of Hellfire - and Anguish's +30% Primary Resource cost needs measuring against a Shock build's mana economy, which is not the same as Firewall's. (5) Re-check at launch. Ball Lightning being made playable is exactly the kind of change that gets tuned between PTR and release.

Incendiary Bolt

PassiveSubo

If Subo's Snipe hits the target he originally aimed at, a Molotov explodes on them.

Ambusher

PassiveSubo

You gain 20%[x] Lucky Hit Chance against enemies damaged by Subo's Salvo within the last 3 seconds.

Share a Drink

PassiveSubo

When one of Subo's Molotovs explodes, it has a 50% chance to drop a Healing Potion for you.

Scorched Earth

PassiveSubo

Subo's initial Molotov explosions cause enemies to take 30%[x] increased Damage Over Time from you for 3 seconds.

Mastermind

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Trap and Trip Mines explosions gain 60% Size.

You and Subo gain 25%[+] Crowd Control Duration.

Loaded Munitions

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Traps and Trip Mines inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 5 seconds.

Opening Fire

PassiveSubo

You deal 25%[x] increased Critical Strike Damage to enemies hit by Subo's Cover Fire for 4 seconds.

Pin Cushion

PassiveSubo

Subo's Cover Fire also Immobilizes enemies for 3 seconds.

Ready At Hand

PassiveSubo

Direct damage to an Elite grants you 20%[+] Movement Speed for 2 seconds.

Piercing Arrows

PassiveSubo

Subo's Heavy Shot now pierces through enemies.

Trip Mines

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 18 seconds

Subo scatters 3 explosive traps that each arm after 1.0 seconds. When an enemy moves within range of one, it explodes for 300% Physical damage and Knocks Down enemies for 1.5 seconds.

Cover Fire

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a countless volley of arrows, then unleashes it over your position for 140% Physical damage that Slows enemies by 50% for 4 seconds.

Explosive Charge

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Subo fires 4 Explosive Charges that stick to enemies. Each explodes after 6.5 seconds or when their target dies, dealing 60% Physical damage.

Snipe

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a massive piercing bolt, then unleashes it forwards for 450% Physical damage that Knocks Back enemies.

Wire Trap

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 10 seconds

Weapon: Bow

Basic Attack: Heavy Shot

Subo places a concussive trap that arms after 0.8 seconds. When an enemy moves within range, it explodes for 80% Physical damage and Stuns enemies for 2.0 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo fires a toughened arrow at an enemy, dealing 80% Physical damage with a 30% chance to Stun for 1.0 seconds.

Molotov

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Crossbow

Basic Attack: Salvo

Subo tosses an incendiary at an enemy, dealing 10% Physical damage and Stunning them for 1.0 seconds before exploding into flames. For the next 5 seconds, enemies within the area repeatedly take 36% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo launches 5 bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Physical damage. The final bolt explodes, Slowing enemies by 50% for 2 seconds.
